context: A uni student interviews a retired archaeologist
purpose: Teach: 亡命/損傷/神聖/考古学/試練/畜産/粒子/仮名

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 考古学の現場、長年携わってこられたんですよね。
lines.en: You've been involved in archaeology fieldwork for quite a long time, haven't you?
lines.style: Respectful, tentative lean-in. Soft onset. The tone of someone genuinely curious but aware he's asking an elder. Slightly formal register — not stiff, but careful.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。神聖視された遺跡で、何度も試練に直面したよ。遺物の損傷を最小化するのに苦労した。
lines.en: Yes. At sites considered sacred, I faced any number of challenges. Minimizing damage to the artifacts was the hardest part.
lines.style: Measured, unhurried. The voice of someone who's earned the right to spare words. Each phrase settles before the next one arrives. Warm but unsentimental — remembering, not lamenting.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 亡命してきた仲間と共同研究もされたとか。
lines.en: I heard you also did collaborative research with colleagues who'd had to leave the country?
lines.style: Careful phrasing — testing whether this is something he'll talk about. Gentle but direct. No presumption in the voice, just genuine interest.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。畜産文化圏とのつながり、貴重だった。
lines.en: Yes. The connections we had with pastoral-culture regions turned out to be invaluable.
lines.style: Quiet warmth on the memory. Slight pause before 'invaluable' — the word carries weight. This was worth the difficulty. Not defensive, just settled.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 粒子分析、当時は難しかったんですか。
lines.en: Was particle analysis particularly difficult to do back then?
lines.style: Genuine scholarly curiosity — no flattery, just asking what he wants to know. Direct but not blunt. The ease of someone in the third hour of a real conversation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ええ、仮名で書かれた古文書の解読も、何年もかかった。
lines.en: Very much so. And deciphering documents written in old phonetic scripts — that alone took years to work through.
lines.style: A slight exhale of acknowledgment before answering. Deliberate pace. The voice settles into authority without strain. Closing note — conclusive but not dismissive. A man who's been patient with this work his whole life.
